$comment: MEMBERSHIP MODULE: the renewal machine (pack: membership). UPSTREAM MAPPING (2026-07-10, bizapps-orders published design): our flat period-per-year rows are the INTERMEDIATE + July-31 shipping shape; the eventual decomposition is one long-lived Subscription per member spawning a renewal Order each cycle (BO-D40/D45). Their design has NO Lapsed/PendingRenewal statuses, NO grace concept, NO AutoRenew flag (auto-renew = stored CustomerPaymentMethod + provider billing) — those are OUR domain rules, later expressed through their SubscriptionEvent stream. Cycle alignment (calendar vs anniversary) is unmodeled upstream — D6 is unconstrained.

tiers.$note: the ACS lattice, verified at source 2026-07-07. Assignment activates the affluence dial: Enthusiast segment → Enthusiast tier; org-backed members climb to business tiers as φ rises; everyone else Individual. Dues ride the tier — so φ becomes OBSERVABLE through tier mix and dues revenue (a copula check the validator can see).
tiers.$assignNote: DECLARED staticAssignment rules (first match wins; last = default) — the affluence dial made observable, now authored here instead of coded in world.mjs

enthusiastRenewal.$note: mirrors benchmarks renewal_rate_enthusiast_tier — the new rule must land this WITHOUT moving the 87% overall (calibration absorbs it)

cancellation.$note: ESTIMATE — the two ways a membership ends. A LAPSE is silence: the renewal never gets paid, grace runs out, staff infer the reason afterwards. A CANCELLATION is a member who TOLD us, mid-term, that they are leaving — the churn a retention team could have worked. Only active-decision reasons qualify (nobody phones in to announce a non-payment), and heroes are excluded so their pinned statuses hold. Before this, all 8,024 periods were Lapsed and the Cancelled value in our own CHECK constraint was never used.

churnReasons.$note: Every lapse used to record a non-payment reason, so the column was useless for a why-are-we-losing-members demo. Real associations lose members for reasons staff record and report on. Non-payment stays the plurality; the employer-event reason is still DERIVED (not drawn) when the member's employer had a lifecycle event.

tenure.label: med
tenure.note: per 1 SD of tenure at decision

engagement.label: strong
engagement.note: latent theta; validated via behavioral proxy (attenuated)

autoRenew.note: HUMAN-AUTHORED FORM + DECLARED FEATURE: members on auto-renew renew about 12 points better — the compiler solves the β; the executor reads the feature from the declaration, not from code

employerEvent.label: med-strong
employerEvent.note: arrow 1.15 — dissolution/acquisition in the decision year. BUILT-IN driver (computed: org lifecycle × decision-year window) — richer than feature grammar v1; migrates when the grammar earns cross-entity time windows

enthusiastTier.note: HUMAN-AUTHORED FORM + DECLARED FEATURE: 'the enthusiast tier renews at about 65%' — compiler solves the β against the calibrated baseline; executor reads the Segment match from the declaration
enthusiastTier.evidence: hobbyist churn is real (AHA analog); benchmarks renewal_rate_enthusiast_tier
